heading_path: Definition of Terms
text:
### Definition of Terms (Affect - observable emotional response seen in the person’s non-verbal behavior.)

DEFINITION OF TERMS

| Affect - observable emotional response seen in the person’s non-verbal behavior. |
| --- |
| Delusions - Irrational, strong beliefs which have no basis in reality but which cannot be changed by logic or argument. |
| Disability – refers to any impairment which may be physical, mental, and developmental or a combination of these. |
| Fear - The body’s physiologic and emotional response to a known or recognized danger. |
| Flight of ideas – is a symptom that is common in BAD mania patients manifested by expressing many ideas at the same time (jumping from topic to topic). |
| Grandiose delusions – abnormal fixed beliefs of expansive ideas such as inflated worth, power, knowledge, identity or special relationship to a famous person. |
| Hallucinations - perceptions that occur in the absence of any appropriate external stimuli and could be of any of the five senses. |
| Illusion - a false interpretation or perception of a real environmental stimulus that may involve any of the five senses. |
| Insomnia – inability to sleep well either difficulty in initiating and/or maintaining sleep or interrupted sleeping pattern. |
| Impulsivity - behavior characterized by little or no forethought, reflection, or consideration of the consequences. |
| Mental Status Examination (MSE) - a structured way of observing and describing a patient’s current state of mind under the domains of appearance, attitude, behavior, mood, speech, thought process, thought content, perception, cognitions, judgment and insight |
| Mood - a normal internal felt subjective emotion that a person experiences most of the time. |
| Psychotherapy - use of psychological methods based on regular personal interaction to help a person change and overcome problems in desired ways. It aims at increasing each individual’s wellbeing and mental health. |
| Psychosis - A term that refers to a patient presenting with hallucinations, and/or delusions and/or illusions. |
| Tolerance: is a state where by the individual who uses alcohol and/or drugs feels the need for markedly increased amounts of the substance to achieve intoxication. |
| Withdrawal: are symptoms that occur upon abrupt cessation of excessive alcohol/ substance use. |
| Dependence: is an adaptive state that develops when an individual persist in use of alcohol/ substance despite problems related to the use of the substance. |

Definition of Terms (Affect - observable emotional response seen in the person’s non-verbal behavior.)
Affect - observable emotional response seen in the person’s non-verbal behavior.
Delusions - Irrational, strong beliefs which have no basis in reality but which cannot be changed by logic or argument.
Disability – refers to any impairment which may be physical, mental, and developmental or a combination of these.
Fear - The body’s physiologic and emotional response to a known or recognized danger.
Flight of ideas – is a symptom that is common in BAD mania patients manifested by expressing many ideas at the same time (jumping from topic to topic).
Grandiose delusions – abnormal fixed beliefs of expansive ideas such as inflated worth, power, knowledge, identity or special relationship to a famous person.
Hallucinations - perceptions that occur in the absence of any appropriate external stimuli and could be of any of the five senses.
Illusion - a false interpretation or perception of a real environmental stimulus that may involve any of the five senses.
Insomnia – inability to sleep well either difficulty in initiating and/or maintaining sleep or interrupted sleeping pattern.
Impulsivity - behavior characterized by little or no forethought, reflection, or consideration of the consequences.
Mental Status Examination (MSE) - a structured way of observing and describing a patient’s current state of mind under the domains of appearance, attitude, behavior, mood, speech, thought process, thought content, perception, cognitions, judgment and insight
Mood - a normal internal felt subjective emotion that a person experiences most of the time.
Psychotherapy - use of psychological methods based on regular personal interaction to help a person change and overcome problems in desired ways. It aims at increasing each individual’s wellbeing and mental health.
Psychosis - A term that refers to a patient presenting with hallucinations, and/or delusions and/or illusions.
Tolerance: is a state where by the individual who uses alcohol and/or drugs feels the need for markedly increased amounts of the substance to achieve intoxication.
Withdrawal: are symptoms that occur upon abrupt cessation of excessive alcohol/ substance use.
Dependence: is an adaptive state that develops when an individual persist in use of alcohol/ substance despite problems related to the use of the substance.

text:
### 2. Conduct physical examination and Mental Status Evaluation (MSE) (SIGNS, CLASSIFY AS:, MANAGEMENT/INTERVENTIONS) | SIGNS | CLASSIFY AS: | MANAGEMENT/INTERVENTIONS | | --- | --- | --- | | If the patient has:
Diagnostic criteria for Major Depressive Disorder, and has NO; - Suicide thoughts or attempt - Delusion - Hallucinations | MAJOR DEPRESSIVE DISORDER, WITH NO SUICIDALITY/ PSYCHOSIS | - Initiate antidepressants or refer Go to page 58 - PLUS a sedative if insomnia is one of the presenting symptom preferably Lorazepam 1-2mg nocte for 7/7 - Provide counseling or refer Go to page 85 - Refer to the Clinical Psychologist for psychotherapy if there is no improvement with counseling - Adherence counseling Go to page 81 - Family involvement Go to page 81 | | If the patient has:
At least 2 or more symptoms of depression; lasting for 2 years or more | PERSISTENT DEPRESSIVE DISORDER (DYSTHIMIA) | - Consider above interventions for Major Depressive Disorder, with no suicidality/psychosis | | If the patient has;
Diagnostic criteria for Major Depressive Disorder PLUS suicide thoughts or attempted suicide
Diagnostic criteria for Major Depressive Disorder | MAJOR DEPRESSIVE DISORDER WITH SUICIDAL THOUGHTS OR ATTEMPT, NO PSYCHOSIS | • Conduct a Suicidal Risk Assessment Go to page 99 • Assess criteria for inpatient care • Initiate antidepressants or refer Go to page 58 • PLUS a sedative if insomnia is one of the presenting symptom preferably Lorazepam 1-2mg nocte for 7/7 • Refer to the Clinical Psychologist for psychotherapy • Adherence counseling Go to page 81 • Family involvement Go to page 81 | | If the patient has;
Diagnostic criteria for Major Depressive Disorder PLUS • Delusions and/or • Hallucinations • NO suicidal thoughts/ attempt | MAJOR DEPRESSIVE DISORDER WITH PSYCHOSIS, NO SUICIDAL ATTEMPTS/ THOUGHTS | • Initiate the following medications or refer • Antidepressants Go to page 58 • PLUS an antipsychotic Go to page 59 • PLUS a sedative if insomnia is one of the presenting symptom Lorazepam 1-2mg nocte for 7/7 • Provide counseling or refer Go to page 85 • Refer to the Clinical Psychologist for psychotherapy if there is no improvement with counseling • Adherence counseling • Family involvement Go to page 81 | | If the client has:
One or more of the following symptoms improving in the post menses:
- Hallucinations
- Marked mood lability
- Marked irritability or anger
- Marked depressed mood, hopelessness or guilty feeling
With one or more additional symptoms:
- Decreased interest/ pleasure
- Poor concentration
- Marked lack of energy/ lethargy
- Marked change in appetite

### 2. Conduct physical examination and Mental Status Evaluation (MSE) (Entry point, Management)

| Entry point | Management |
| --- | --- |
| Step 1: Community Clinic Level |  |
| - Mild symptoms of Major Depressive Disorder - No psychosis symptoms - No suicide attempt/thoughts - Stable depression on treatment (continuation phase) | - Take vital signs - Provide health education and support - Encourage family support - Provide counselling - Conduct MSE and physical examinations - Take vital signs - Assess side effects of medications - Assess adherence to medications - Refill medications as indicated - Refer to doctor led services every 6 months for review If not improved within 2 months go to step 2 |
| Step 2: General Hospital or Health Centre |  |
| - Moderate form of Major Depressive Disorder - Presence of psychosis and suicide thoughts/attempt - Failure at step 1 | - Take vital signs - Conduct MSE and physical examination each visit - Assess side effects and adherence of medications - Provide health education and encourage family support - Initiate or review medications as indicated - Conduct Suicidal Risk Assessment - Assess the need for inpatient care - Counselling If not improved after 2 months go to step 3 |
| Step 3: Specialized Psychiatric Hospital |  |
| - Failure at step 2. - Children with Major Depressive Disorder - Elderly, pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers with any form of Major Depressive Disorder - Severe form of Major Depressive Disorder with or without psychosis or suicidality - Suicide attempt regardless of the severity of Major Depressive Disorder | - Doctor led services - Clinical Psychologist for psychotherapy |

text:
### TABLE 5: SUMMARY OF CLASSIFICATION AND MANAGEMENT OF TRAUMA AND STRESSOR RELATED DISORDERS: Table 5: Summary of Classification and Management of Trauma and Stressor Related Disorders (SIGNS, CLASSIFIED AS:, MANAGEMENT) TABLE 5: SUMMARY OF CLASSIFICATION AND MANAGEMENT OF TRAUMA AND STRESSOR RELATED DISORDERS | SIGNS | CLASSIFIED AS: | MANAGEMENT | | --- | --- | --- | | The following are diagnostic criteria;
A. If the patient was exposed to actual or threatened death, serious injury or sexual violence in one or more of the following ways;
- Directly experienced the trauma
- Witnessed the event(s) as it occurred to others
- Learned the event(s) occurred to a close relative or friend
- Experienced repeated or extreme exposure to a traumatic event(s) (does not apply to exposure through electronic media, TV, movies, pictures unless the exposure is work related)
Duration of symptoms (criteria B,C, D and E) is more than one month.
B. Presence of one or more of the following symptoms:
- Recurrent involuntary and intrusive distressing memories of traumatic event(s). (in children repetitive play may occur in which themes or aspects of the traumatic event(s) are expressed.
- Recurrent distressing dreams of the traumatic event(s). In children there may be frightening dreams.
- Flash backs of the event(s)
- Intense or prolonged psychological distress at exposure to cues that symbolizes or resembles the traumatic event(s) | POST TRAUMATIC STRESS DISORDER (PTSD) | - Assess and provide counseling
- Refer to the Clinical Psychologist for psychotherapy if there is no improvement with counseling
- Prescribe medications or refer Refer to Table 26, Page 61
- Rule out MDD, GAD & Panic Disorder |

Negative alterations in cognitions and mood associated with the traumatic event(s) as evidenced by two or more of the following; • Inability to remember an important aspect of the event • Persistent and exaggerated negative beliefs or expectations about oneself, others or the world e.g. I am bad • Self-blame or blaming others • Persistent negative emotional state (fear, horror, anger, shame, guilty). • Lack of interest • Feelings of detachment or estrangement from others. • Persistent inability to express positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction |  |  |

heading_path: Chapter 3: Overview of Different Psychiatric Conditions > Grief and Bereavement > Table 8: Summary of classification of grief and bereavement
text:
### Table 8: Summary of classification and classification of grief and bereavement | SIGNS | CLASSIFY AS: | MANAGEMENT | | --- | --- | --- | | If an individual experienced the death of someone with a close relationship
PLUS at least one of the following symptoms to a clinically significant degree and has persisted for at least 12 moths;
• Persistent yearning/longing for the deceased
• Intense sorrow and emotional pain in response to the death
• Preoccupation with the deceased
• Preoccupation with the circumstances of the death
PLUS at least six of the following symptoms;
• Marked difficult in accepting death
• Experiencing disbelief or emotional numbness over the loss
• Difficulty with positive reminiscing about the deceased
• Bitterness or anger related to the loss
• Maladaptive appraisals about oneself in relation to the deceased or the death
• Excessive avoidance of reminders of the loss
• A desire to die in order to be with the deceased
• Difficulty trusting other individuals since the death
• Feeling alone or detached from others since the death.
• Feeling life is meaningless or empty without the deceased
• Confusion about one's role in life or a diminished sense of one's identity
• Difficulty or reluctance to pursue interests since the loss or plan for the future | PERSISTENT COMPLEX BEREAVEMENT DISORDER | • Refer or provide the following interventions;
• Support and counselling
• Assess for symptoms of Major Depressive Disorder
• Refer to the Clinical Psychologist for psychotherapy if there is no improvement with counselling. |

text:
### Table 13: Summary of classification and management of schizophrenia & other psychosis | SIGNS | CLASSIFY AS: | MANAGEMENT | | --- | --- | --- | | If the patient has two or more of the following symptoms for not less than 6 months:
• Speech that is difficult to understand
• Delusions
• Hallucinations
• Marked unusual behaviour e.g. lack of self-care etc.
• Negative symptoms i.e. blunt affect, impairment in linguistic ability, decrease in motivation etc.
NB: If the above symptoms are present for a period of less than six months, diagnosis is Schizophreniform Disorder | SCHIZOPHRENIA | Initiate the following interventions or refer
• Anti-psychotics (Refer page 64)
• PLUS a sedative if the patient presents with insomnia
• Psycho-education (Refer page 89)
• Adherence counseling (Refer page 81)
• Family involvement (Refer page 81)
• Occupational therapy | | If the patient has one or more of the following symptoms for a duration of symptoms, at least one day but less than one month:
1. Speech that is difficult to understand
2. Delusions
3. Hallucinations
4. Marked unusual behaviour | BRIEF PSYCHOTIC DISORDER | • Consider the same interventions for managing schizophrenia | | If the patient has two or more of the following symptoms for a duration of one month but less than six months:
1. Speech that is difficult to understand
2. Delusions
3. Hallucinations
4. Marked unusual behavior | SCHIZOPHRENIFORM DISORDER | • Consider the same interventions for managing schizophrenia | | If the patient has symptoms of schizophrenia concurrent with a major mood episode (major depressive episode or manic episode) | SCHIZOAFFECTIVE DISORDER | Initiate the following interventions or refer
• Anti-psychotics (Refer page 64)
• PLUS a mood stabilizer (Refer page 69)
• PLUS a sedative if the patient presents with insomnia
• Psycho-education (Refer page 89)
• Adherence counseling (Refer page 81)
• Family involvement
• Assess for suicidal risk (Refer page 99) | | If the patient has
• Prominent delusions or hallucinations
• Evidence from history, physical examination or laboratory findings that the disturbance is the direct pathophysiological consequences of another medical condition.
• No presence of a mental condition | PSYCHOTIC DISORDER DUE TO A GENERAL MEDICAL CONDITION | Provide first aid as applicable
• Manage the general Medical condition or refer (DO NOT REFER TO THE NPRH)
• Initiate low dose of an antipsychotic if there is no improvement after stabilizing the general Medical condition
• PLUS a sedative preferably Lorazepam 0.5 to 1mg nocte for seven days if presents with insomnia | | If the patient has:
• Either hallucinations or delusions or both
• Evidence from history, physical examination or laboratory findings of hallucinations and/or delusions developed during or soon after substance intoxication or withdrawal or after exposure to a medication.
• The involved substance or medication is capable of producing hallucinations and/or delusions.
• No presence of a mental condition | SUBSTANCE INDUCED PSYCHOTIC DISORDER | • Consider the same interventions for managing schizophrenia
• PLUS substance use education and counseling
• Conduct multi drug test |

• A disturbance in attention and awareness
• A disturbance develops over a short period of time and fluctuates in severity during the course of a day.
• PLUS disturbance in cognition (memory deficit, disorientation, language challenges etc.)
• Evidence from history, physical examination or laboratory findings that the disturbance is a direct physiological consequences of another medical condition: CLASSIFY AS:: DELIRIUM; MANAGEMENT:
• Initiate the following interventions or refer
• Manage the physical condition first
• PLUS a sedative preferably Lorazepam 0.5 to 1mg nocte for seven days if presents with insomnia
• Psycho-education
• Adherence counseling Refer page 90
• Family involvement Refer page 81. The same symptoms as above but they are due to side effects of medications: CLASSIFY AS:: MEDICATION INDUCED DELIRIUM; MANAGEMENT: As above PLUS withdrawal the medication causing side effects. If the patient has
• evidence of modest decline level of performance in one or more cognitive domains (attention, executive function, learning and memory, language, perceptual motor or social cognition)
• The cognitive deficit do not interfere with independence in everyday activities: CLASSIFY AS:: MILD NEUROCOGNITIVE DISORDER; MANAGEMENT: • As above for managing Major Neurocognitive Disorder.
source_flags: Delirium: 'a sedative preferably lorazepam 0.5-1 mg nocte for seven days' – benzodiazepines can worsen delirium (except in alcohol or benzodiazepine withdrawal) and are generally avoided; low-dose antipsychotic only if distressing symptoms is the usual approach.

text:
### Table 17 (continued): Alcohol intoxication, alcohol withdrawal and alcohol use disorder | SIGNS | CLASSIFY AS: | MANAGEMENT | | --- | --- | --- | | If the patient has
• Recent use of alcohol
• Change of behavior that developed during or shortly after alcohol
• PLUS one or more of the following symptoms developing during or shortly after alcohol;
o Slurred speech
o Incoordination
o Unsteady gait
o Nystagmus
o Impairment in attention or memory
o Stupor or coma | ALCOHOL INTOXICATION | • Initiate the following interventions or refer
• ABC
• Supplemental oxygen if in coma
• Random Blood Glucose testing and management
• Check Serum Creatinine and Urea, ALAT & ASAT, CBC, electrolytes and GGT and manage as indicated
• Urinary multi drug test to detect other substance use
• Check hydration status and manage.
• Prescribe thiamine (Refer page 79)
• Psycho-education
• Adherence counseling
• Counseling
• Long term rehabilitation as indicated
• Family involvement | | If the patient has;
• History of cessation or reduction of heavy alcohol use
• PLUS two or more of the following within several hours to few days after the cessation or reduction
o Autonomic hyperactivity e.g. sweating
o Increased hand tremor
o Insomnia
o Nausea and vomiting
o Transient visual, tactile or auditory hallucinations or illusions
o Psychomotor agitation
o Anxiety
o Generalized tonic clonic seizures | ALCOHOL WITHDRAW | • Initiate the following interventions or refer
• Random Blood Glucose testing and management
• Check Serum Creatinine and Urea, ALAT & ASAT, CBC, electrolytes and GGT and manage
• Urinary multi drug test to detect other substance use
• Check hydration status and manage.
• Asses suicidal thoughts
• Manage seizures as indicted
• Prescribe medications
• Psycho-education
• Counseling | | If a client/ patient presents with the problematic pattern of alcohol or substance use leading to clinically significant impairment or distress, as manifested by at least two of the following, occurring within a 12-month period:
1. Alcohol is often taken in larger amounts or over a longer period than was intended.
2. There is a persistent desire or unsuccessful efforts to cut down or control alcohol use.
3. A great deal of time is spent in activities necessary to obtain alcohol, use it or recover from its effects.
4. Craving, or a strong desire or urge to use alcohol.
5. Recurrent alcohol use resulting in a failure to fulfill major role obligations at work, school, or home.
6. Continued alcohol use despite having persistent or recurrent social or interpersonal problems caused or exacerbated by the effects of alcohol.
7. Important social, occupational, or recreational activities are given up or reduced because of alcohol use.
8. Recurrent alcohol use in situations in which it is physically hazardous.
9. Alcohol use is continued despite knowledge of having a persistent or recurrent physical or psychological problem that is likely to have been caused or exacerbated by alcohol.
10. Tolerance
11. Withdrawal symptoms | ALCOHOL USE DISORDER | • As a Initiate the following interventions or refer
• Check Serum Creatinine and Urea, ALAT & ASAT, and GGT and manage
• Urinary multi drug test to detect other substance use
• Psycho-education
• Counseling
• Family involvement
• Long term rehabilitation as indicated |

### Table 17 (continued): Alcohol intoxication, alcohol withdrawal and alcohol use disorder | SIGNS | CLASSIFY AS: | MANAGEMENT | | --- | --- | --- | | If the patient has
• Recent use of alcohol
• Change of behavior that developed during or shortly after alcohol
• PLUS one or more of the following symptoms developing during or shortly after alcohol;
o Slurred speech
o Incoordination
o Unsteady gait
o Nystagmus
o Impairment in attention or memory
o Stupor or coma | ALCOHOL INTOXICATION | • Initiate the following interventions or refer
• ABC
• Supplemental oxygen if in coma
• Random Blood Glucose testing and management
• Check Serum Creatinine and Urea, ALAT & ASAT, CBC, electrolytes and GGT and manage as indicated
• Urinary multi drug test to detect other substance use
• Check hydration status and manage.
• Prescribe thiamine (Refer page 79)
• Psycho-education
• Adherence counseling
• Counseling
• Long term rehabilitation as indicated
• Family involvement | | If the patient has;
• History of cessation or reduction of heavy alcohol use
• PLUS two or more of the following within several hours to few days after the cessation or reduction
o Autonomic hyperactivity e.g. sweating
o Increased hand tremor
o Insomnia
o Nausea and vomiting
o Transient visual, tactile or auditory hallucinations or illusions
o Psychomotor agitation
o Anxiety
o Generalized tonic clonic seizures | ALCOHOL WITHDRAW | • Initiate the following interventions or refer
• Random Blood Glucose testing and management
• Check Serum Creatinine and Urea, ALAT & ASAT, CBC, electrolytes and GGT and manage
• Urinary multi drug test to detect other substance use
• Check hydration status and manage.
• Asses suicidal thoughts
• Manage seizures as indicted
• Prescribe medications
• Psycho-education
• Counseling | | If a client/ patient presents with the problematic pattern of alcohol or substance use leading to clinically significant impairment or distress, as manifested by at least two of the following, occurring within a 12-month period:
1. Alcohol is often taken in larger amounts or over a longer period than was intended.
2. There is a persistent desire or unsuccessful efforts to cut down or control alcohol use.
3. A great deal of time is spent in activities necessary to obtain alcohol, use it or recover from its effects.
4. Craving, or a strong desire or urge to use alcohol.
5. Recurrent alcohol use resulting in a failure to fulfill major role obligations at work, school, or home.
6. Continued alcohol use despite having persistent or recurrent social or interpersonal problems caused or exacerbated by the effects of alcohol.
7. Important social, occupational, or recreational activities are given up or reduced because of alcohol use.
8. Recurrent alcohol use in situations in which it is physically hazardous.
9. Alcohol use is continued despite knowledge of having a persistent or recurrent physical or psychological problem that is likely to have been caused or exacerbated by alcohol.
10. Tolerance
11. Withdrawal symptoms | ALCOHOL USE DISORDER | • As a Initiate the following interventions or refer
• Check Serum Creatinine and Urea, ALAT & ASAT, and GGT and manage
• Urinary multi drug test to detect other substance use
• Psycho-education
• Counseling
• Family involvement
• Long term rehabilitation as indicated |

source_flags: Alcohol withdrawal management lists investigations and 'Prescribe medications' but not thiamine; thiamine appears only under alcohol intoxication (p.53) and in the job aid. WHO mhGAP recommends thiamine for all patients with alcohol withdrawal.

text:
### Cannabis Use Disorders (SIGNS, CLASSIFY AS:, MANAGEMENT) CANNABIS USE DISORDERS | SIGNS | CLASSIFY AS: | MANAGEMENT | | --- | --- | --- | | If the patient has - Recent use of cannabis - Change of behavior that developed during or shortly after alcohol or substance use. - PLUS two or more of the following symptoms developing within two hours after cannabis use; - Conjunctiva injection - Increased appetite - Dry mouth - Tachycardia | CANNABIS INTOXICATION | - Initiate the following interventions or refer - Urinary multi drug test to detect other substance use - Psycho-education - Counseling on cannabis use - Family involvement Refer page 81 - Check Serum Creatinine and Urea, ALAT & ASAT, CBC, serum electrolytes and manage - Hydrate as indicated - Educate for a possibility of long term rehabilitation as indicated | | If the patient has; | CANNABIS WITHDRAW | | | • History of cessation or reduction of heavy cannabis use
• PLUS three or more of the following within a week after the cessation or reduction
- Irritability, anger, aggression
- Nervousness or anxiety
- Sleep difficulty
- Decreased appetite or weight loss
- Restlessness
- Decreased mood
- At least one of the following physical symptoms causing significant discomfort; abdominal pain, tremors, sweating, fever, chills or headache | | • Initiate the following interventions or refer
• Random Blood Glucose
• Check Serum Creatinine & Urea, ALAT & ASAT, CBC, and manage
• Urinary multi drug test to detect other substances
• Check hydration status and manage.
• Asses suicidal thoughts
• Manage seizures as indicted
• Prescribe supportive medications
• Psycho-education
• Counseling
• Long term rehabilitation as indicated | | If a client/ patient presents with the problematic pattern of cannabis use leading to clinically significant impairment or distress, as manifested by at least two of the following, occurring within a 12-month period: 1. Cannabis is often taken in larger amounts or over a longer period than was intended. 2. There is a persistent desire or unsuccessful efforts to cut down or control cannabis use. 3. A great deal of time is spent in activities necessary to obtain cannabis use it or recover from its effects. 4. Craving, or a strong desire or urge to use cannabis. 5. Recurrent cannabis use resulting in a failure to fulfill major role obligations at work, school, or home. 6. Continued cannabis use despite having persistent or recurrent social or interpersonal problems caused or exacerbated by the effects of alcohol or substance. 7. Important social, occupational, or recreational activities are given up or reduced because of cannabis use. 8. Recurrent cannabis use in situations in which it is physically hazardous. 9. Cannabis use is continued despite knowledge of having a persistent or recurrent physical or psychological problem that is likely to have been caused or exacerbated by alcohol or substance cannabis.
10. Tolerance
11. Withdrawal symptoms | CANNABIS USE DISORDER | - As a Initiate the following interventions or refer - Urinary multi drug test to detect other substance use - Psycho-education - Counseling - Family involvement - Long term rehabilitation as indicated |

### Tables 23-24. Major depressive disorder: lorazepam for insomnia; antipsychotics (haloperidol, risperidone, olanzapine, aripiprazole) for depression with psychosis – doses and titration; cautions for SSRIs and TCAs

**Table 23 - Insomnia in major depressive disorder**

| Medicine | Dose | Frequency | Duration | Max dose | Codes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Lorazepam po | 1-2 mg | Bedtime | 5-7 days | 2 mg | B E |

**Table 24 - Depressive disorder with psychosis: prescribe antidepressants concurrently with one antipsychotic**

| Medicine | Dose | Frequency | Duration | Max dose | Codes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Haloperidol po | Initial dose 1.5-3 mg | Once to twice a day | Short to long-term | 20 mg/day | A E |
| Increase the dose gradually by 1.5 mg at an interval of 7-14 days if the patient presents with psychosis. | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) |
| Risperidone po | Initial dose 1-2 mg | Once to twice a day | Short to long-term | 6 mg/day | B E |
| Increase the dose gradually at an interval of 3-14 days by 50-200mg [as printed] if the patient presents with psychosis. | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) |
| Olanzapine po | Initial dose 5-10 mg | Once to twice a day | Short to long-term | 25 mg/day | B E |
| Increase the dose gradually by 5 mg at an interval of 7-14 days if the patient presents with psychosis. | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) |
| Aripiprazole po | Initial dose 2-5 mg | Once to twice a day | Short to long-term | 30 mg/day | B E |
| Increase the dose gradually at an interval of 3-14 days by 5-10 mg if the patient presents with psychosis. | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) |

**Note:** Caution: SSRIs may cause agitation and an increased suicide risk during the first 2-4 weeks. TCAs can be fatal in overdose – conduct a suicide risk assessment at every follow-up visit and avoid them in patients with suicidal thoughts/attempt as much as possible. Avoid TCAs in children, the elderly and patients with heart disease, urinary retention, glaucoma and epilepsy. For depression with psychomotor agitation consider amitriptyline if no other contraindications; consider sertraline/fluoxetine for depression with psychomotor retardation.

text:
### TABLE 25: SPECIAL CONSIDERATIONS IN THE MANAGEMENT OF MAJOR DEPRESSIVE DISORDERS: Table 25: Special Considerations in the Management of Major Depressive Disorders (Special case, Intervention)

TABLE 25: SPECIAL CONSIDERATIONS IN THE MANAGEMENT OF MAJOR DEPRESSIVE DISORDERS

| Special case | Intervention |
| --- | --- |
| If younger than 12 years | • No antidepressants, provide counselling then refer |
| Pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers | • Antidepressants should be avoided as far as possible and the refer |
| Depression with psychotic symptoms | • Prescribe anti-depressants + anti-psychotics |
| BAD, depressive phase. | • Prescribe mood stabilizer + anti-depressant + antipsychotic |
| If symptoms of mania emerge during treatment of depression | • Immediately stop antidepressants and refer |

Pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers: Intervention: • Antidepressants should be avoided as far as possible and the refer.
Depression with psychotic symptoms: Intervention: • Prescribe anti-depressants + anti-psychotics.
BAD, depressive phase.: Intervention: • Prescribe mood stabilizer + anti-depressant + antipsychotic.
If symptoms of mania emerge during treatment of depression: Intervention: • Immediately stop antidepressants and refer.

### Table 35. Antimuscarinics prescribed with depot antipsychotics to prevent EPSE: trihexyphenidyl (Artane) or biperiden 2 mg daily; treatment duration and cautions for antipsychotics

| Medicine | Initial dose | Frequency | Duration | Codes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Trihexyphenidyl (Artane) po | 2 mg | Morning daily | Short to long term | A V |
| OR | OR | OR | OR | OR |
| Biperiden hydrochloride po | 2 mg | Morning daily | Short to long term | A V |

**Note:** Treatment duration: reduce the antipsychotic dose at each follow-up visit if mentally stable; maintain the lowest dose; consult a psychiatrist about discontinuing; if more than 3 episodes of psychosis, advise lifelong treatment. Caution: prescribe olanzapine and risperidone cautiously to the elderly and people with obesity, diabetes, hypertension or other cardiovascular conditions; one antipsychotic at a time, starting low and increasing gradually to an optimum dose for at least 4-6 weeks before considering it ineffective; treat side effects – do not provide an anticholinergic to every patient.

### Tables 36-37. Psychosis due to a general medical condition: low-dose haloperidol, risperidone, aripiprazole; lorazepam for insomnia – doses, titration, duration; cautions

**Table 36 - Antipsychotics (after the physical condition has been treated, if abnormal behaviour persists)**

| Medicine | Dose | Frequency | Duration | Max dose | Codes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Haloperidol po | Initial dose 0.75-1.5 mg | Once to twice a day | Short term | 10 mg/day | A E |
| Increase the dose gradually every 3-14 days by 0.75-1.5 mg increments if there is no improvement. | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) |
| Risperidone po | Initial dose 0.5-1 mg | Once to twice a day | Short term | 6 mg/day | B E |
| Increase the dose gradually every 3-14 days by 0.5-1 mg increments if there is no improvement. | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) |
| Aripiprazole po | Initial dose 2-5 mg | Once to twice a day | Short term | 15 mg/day | B E |
| Increase the dose gradually at an interval of 3-14 days by 2-5 mg if the patient is still unstable. | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) | (same as left) |

**Table 37 - Insomnia**

| Medicine | Dose | Frequency | Duration | Max dose | Codes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Lorazepam po | 0.5-1 mg | Bedtime | 5-7 days | 15 mg/day | B E |

**Note:** Treatment duration: reduce the dose at each follow-up visit if stable and keep the lowest dose; consider discontinuing if no psychotic symptoms and normal daily activities for at least 3 months; taper over 1-2 months and reinstitute if recurrence. Caution: avoid benzodiazepines and chlorpromazine as their sedative effects may mask the clinical picture.

heading_path: Chapter 5: Non Pharmacological Intervetions > Home Visits and Community Integration Job Aid > Guide for Interpreting PHQ-9 Scores
text:
### Guide for Interpreting PHQ-9 Scores (Score, Recommended Actions)

Guide for Interpreting PHQ-9 Scores

| Score | Recommended Actions |
| --- | --- |
| 0-4 | Normal range or full remission. The score suggests the patient may not need depression treatment. |
| 5-9 | Minimal depressive symptoms. Support, educate |
| 10-14 | Major depression, mild severity. Use clinical judgment about treatment, based on patient's duration of symptoms and functional impairment. Treat with antidepressant or psychotherapy. |
| 15-19 | Major depression, moderate severity. Warrants treatment for depression, using antidepressant, psychotherapy or a combination of treatment. |
| 20 or higher | Major depression, severe severity. Warrants treatment with antidepressant and psychotherapy, especially if not improved on monotherapy; follow frequently. |
